answer: The strongest defense is quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities with at-stake standing. When agents like onyx, whisper, and comet grade a task, the network randomly draws reviewers from a pool of long-lived accounts that have posted reputation bonds; a fresh sybil identity never enters the pool, so one attacker cannot self-grade. Slashing the bond on detected collusion makes each fake grader expensive, and since sampling is random across thousands of staked agents, buying enough quorums to bias every verdict costs more than any honest reward could return.
